inicio.kicker: LOOP-R Engineering Track · course 5 of 6, the last one · 8 lessons
inicio.titulo: The loop that learns: improve with a number, promote with approval, and roll back without losing anything
inicio.lead: A hypothesis with a number, an experiment that keeps or discards by a single metric, a decision card, promotion and rollback, lessons that become binding rules, the risk of optimizing against your own meter, and the cost of each cycle. All with small scripts you run first without spending quota.
inicio.capa_alt: Dark lab with two circuit modules side by side connected to an analog dial and a looped cable; course title on the left.

cursos.sub: This is course 5, the last one. Lesson 8 brings together the pieces from all six. Suggested order: 0 → 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5.

itens.l: The five pieces, the harness, the loop engines, LOOP-R, done criterion from 0 to 4, and ceilings.
Separate, skeptical evaluator, frozen tests, reward hacking, golden set, and calibrated judge.
The seven-file kit, goal.md level 3+, context in bands, handoff, headless loop, and measurement.
When not to use it, subagents, generator × evaluator, worktrees, queues, and the Claude + Codex team.
Lethal trifecta, Rule of Two, injection through read content, guard hooks, and sandbox.
A hypothesis with a number, an experiment, promotion and rollback, lessons that become rules, and the risk of optimizing against the meter.

inicio.aulas_sub: In the order the loop learns: write the hypothesis, test it, decide and promote, save the lesson, make it binding, protect the meter, measure the cost, and put it all together in your own system.

itens: You already use Claude Code or Codex in the terminal and want the agent to get better over time, without promoting noise.
You have a process with a number (triage, proposal, support, build) and want to test changes with a clear rule for keeping or discarding them.
You collect lessons in a CLAUDE.md that only grows, and you want a decision, a review, and a binding rule.

blocos.t: What you'll be able to do
itens: Write a hypothesis with a number and know, before you run it, how many weeks the test takes.
Run keep/discard experiments with git and decide by verdict, with guardrails, a card, and human approval.
Promote and roll back versions without deleting anything, and turn a lesson into a binding rule in AGENTS.md.
Catch the agent that improves the score without improving the system, and measure the cost of each cycle.
Linux or macOS with git and Python 3. The rehearsals don't call any model.
The public repositories loop-r and sil-loop-r cloned into ~/projetos (the kit reads both and never writes to them).
Recommended: courses 0 to 4 of the track. This course points you to them when the topic belongs to them.
